title: Ubuntu Linux Kernel Test Engineer
description:
Ubuntu is the most widely used Linux distribution in the world, delivering kernels across a vast matrix of versions, architectures, and configurations – with up to 15 years of security and maintenance commitments for Long Term Support (LTS) releases. Ensuring the quality and reliability of these kernels demands a dedicated, systematic approach to testing at scale.

The Canonical Kernel Team is looking for a Test Engineer to take ownership of our kernel testing strategy and infrastructure. You will design and maintain test plans covering functional correctness, stability, performance, and security. You will build and evolve automated test frameworks – including stress testing, fuzzing, code coverage analysis, and regression detection – that not only must remain effective across many concurrently supported kernel versions spanning years of maintenance, but must be able to scale with the high demand for Ubuntu kernels (currently more than 160 under active support).

The successful candidate will bring strong Python skills, familiarity with Linux kernel internals, and experience building test infrastructure that scales. You will work closely with kernel engineers to catch regressions early, validate fixes, and ensure every kernel we ship meets the highest standards of reliability.

Location: This role will be based remotely in the APAC region, except for Taipei, Taiwan, and Beijing, China, which are office-based locations.

What your day will look like

- Design, develop, and maintain comprehensive test plans covering functional correctness, stability, performance, and security for Ubuntu Linux kernels

- Build and improve automated test infrastructure for continuous kernel quality validation across multiple kernel versions and architectures

- Maintain long-lived test suites that evolve alongside Ubuntu’s many concurrently supported kernel versions spanning years of maintenance

- Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines for continuous kernel quality validation

- Conduct performance benchmarking and regression detection across kernel releases

- Measure and improve kernel code coverage, identifying gaps in test coverage and creating tests to address them

- Execute and analyze stress tests covering CPU scheduling, memory management, I/O subsystems, networking, and filesystem workloads

- Develop and maintain fuzzing harnesses to discover kernel vulnerabilities and reliability issues using tools such as syzkaller, Trinity, or custom fuzzers

- Collaborate regularly and proactively with a globally distributed team

- Contribute to upstream test suites and testing frameworks

- Document test methodologies, results, and coverage gaps

What we are looking for in you

- Significant programming experience in Python

- Experience with test frameworks such as LTP, kselftest, xfstests, stress-ng, fio, or similar

- Experience designing and executing system-level tests: functional, stress, performance, or regression testing

- Familiarity with CI/CD systems (Jenkins, GitHub CI, or similar)

- Experience maintaining test suites over long periods, adapting to evolving software across multiple supported versions

- Familiarity with Linux (Ubuntu or Debian preferred but not required), Linux kernel internals and subsystems

- Experience with Linux systems administration and automation

- Solid background with git

- Well-organized, self-starting and able to deliver to fixed schedules

- Professional written and spoken English with excellent communication skills

- Ability to travel twice a year, for company events up to two weeks each

Additional skills that you might also bring

- Familiarity with kernel fuzzing tools and techniques (e.g. syzkaller, Trinity, AFL, or custom harnesses)

- Experience with code coverage instrumentation (e.g. gcov, kcov, LLVM source-based coverage)

- Knowledge of kernel tracing and observability tools (e.g. ftrace, perf, bpftrace, eBPF)

- Familiarity with static analysis tools (e.g. sparse, smatch, Coccinelle) as part of a testing workflow

- Experience with fault injection frameworks (e.g. failslab, fail_make_request) for reliability testing

- Prior experience with test infrastructure at scale (provisioning, orchestration, result aggregation)

- Experience with Ubuntu/Debian packaging or Snap

- Knowledge of virtualization technologies (KVM, QEMU) and container runtimes

- Cloud infrastructure experience (AWS, GCP, Azure, or OpenStack)

- Prior involvement with open source testing communities or projects

What we offer you

Your base pay will depend on various factors including your geographical location, level of experience, knowledge and skills. In addition to the benefits above, certain roles are also eligible for additional benefits and rewards including annual bonuses and sales incentives based on revenue or utilisation. Our compensation philosophy is to ensure equity right across our global workforce. 

In addition to a competitive base pay, we provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. Please note that additional benefits may apply depending on the work location and, for more information on these, you can ask in the later stages of the recruitment process.

- Fully remote working environment - we’ve been working remotely since 2004!

- Personal learning and development budget of 2,000USD per annum

- Annual compensation review

- Recognition rewards

- Annual holiday leave

- Parental Leave

- Employee Assistance Programme

- Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues at ‘sprints’

- Priority Pass for travel and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical 

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm that is at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do.

Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Work at Canonical is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical provides a unique window into the world of 21st-century digital business.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer 

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

You will work closely with cross-functional teams (embedded, software, and hardware) to design, develop, and deploy advanced algorithms that predict energy infrastructure failures.

Previous experience in partial discharge, acoustic emission or electrical signal processing is an advantage, but not a dealbreaker. We value strong analytical thinking, curiosity, and the willingness to learn new domains.

- Design, develop, validate, and maintain algorithms for sensor data analysis, partial-discharge monitoring, and predictive analytics.

- Translate complex business and engineering requirements into robust, production-ready algorithms.

- Analyse large-scale sensor, time-series, and operational datasets to identify meaningful patterns and improve monitoring platform performance

- Develop signal-processing, feature-engineering, statistical-modelling, and machine-learning pipelines.

- Collaborate with software and platform engineers to integrate algorithms into the cloud monitoring platform and edge environments.

- Monitor deployed algorithm performance and contribute to model maintenance, retraining, and continuous improvement.

- Join one of Europe’s most promising deep-tech scale-ups.

- Competitive salary and benefits package.

Requirements:

- Strong professional experience with Python and commonly used scientific and data-science libraries (e.g., pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn).

- Strong foundation in statistical analysis, algorithm development, machine learning, and data modelling.

- Practical experience analysing sensor signals and time-series data.

- Solid understanding of signal-processing techniques such as filtering, denoising, spectral analysis, Fourier or wavelet transforms, and dimensionality reduction.

- Experience developing, validating, and deploying machine-learning models in production or cloud environments.

- Ability to connect patterns in data with physical processes and real-world system behaviour.

- Experience with at least one deep-learning framework, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX.

- Ability to write clear, modular, tested, and maintainable Python code.

title: Senior ML Engineer | Kimchi (Inference Stack Optimization)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and we run the models underneath it ourselves.

Kimchi Inference 

One API line and a customer's existing client just works: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Nemotron served serverless from our own GPU fleet (OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible, pay per token, spend visible per user, team, and key). When control matters, the same models run on the customer's own cluster instead. Behind that one line sits the machinery you'll own: SGLang and vLLM engines, B300 nodes, a shared cluster filesystem that holds every checkpoint exactly once, KV caches riding coding traffic with heavy prefix reuse, and the benchmark harness that gates every change we ship.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Throughput. Latency. Cold starts. Cost per token.

Move those four numbers in the right direction and two things happen: customers get faster, cheaper inference, and our margins improve. That's the entire thesis of this role. Every loader you tune, every scheduler decision you land, every kernel you stare at shows up in a customer's p99 and on our P&L. Your mandate is the inference stack's optimization, whatever it takes, and the technical direction of how we optimize it is yours to argue with data.

The problem: the checkpoints run 0.3-1.5 TB, and the "right" serving configuration depends on traffic shape, sequence-length distribution, batch dynamics, GPU SKU, memory bandwidth, and quantization tolerance, all variables that shift week to week. Most teams pick a configuration once, over-provision GPUs, and absorb the cost. We don't: we took Kimi-K3 (1.5 TB) from over an hour cold-to-serving to under twelve minutes with a shared filesystem, O_DIRECT weight loaders, and node-local JIT caches, and we're nowhere near done. Prefill/decode disaggregation and tiered KV caches are next.

Stack: Python; SGLang; vLLM; TensorRT-LLM; PyTorch; fastsafetensors; CUDA-adjacent tooling; Kubernetes; virtiofs shared filesystems; ClickHouse; OpenTelemetry; Prometheus; Grafana; GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've built real ML systems for 5+ years, and your portfolio shows depth in inference or training infrastructure, not just model training notebooks.

- Your Python is production-grade: services, not scripts.

- You've run vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM for real, and you have a working mental model of why an engine performs the way it does on a given GPU.

- You've measured quantization regressions, not just compression ratios.

- Multi-GPU and multi-node setups hold no fear: tensor and expert parallelism, collective communication, and their practical failure modes.

- You know where the bytes live (page caches, O_DIRECT, network filesystems under terabyte-scale reads) and how fast they move.

- You instrument before you optimize, and you can tell a real win from a benchmark artifact.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

- Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

- Push throughput. Continuous batching, chunked prefill, speculative decoding with draft models, CUDA-graph capture, and scheduler tuning across the engine
fleet. Find the ceiling on each GPU SKU, then raise it.

- Cut latency. Attack TTFT and inter-token latency separately; profile to find the actual bottleneck (compute, memory bandwidth, scheduling, storage, or
network) and fix it, not the one you assumed.

- Get more out of the KV cache. Hierarchical and paged attention, prefix caching on heavy-reuse coding traffic, eviction policies, quantized KV. A lot of the
unrealized throughput lives here, and you'll own it.

- Kill cold starts. Weight loaders (O_DIRECT, fastsafetensors-class), JIT and compile caches, shared-filesystem read paths. A 1.5 TB checkpoint has no business
taking an hour to reach serving.

- Quantize without regressing quality. INT8/INT4, FP8/FP4 across weights, activations, and KV, measured on real workloads, not just perplexity benchmarks.

- Scale across nodes. Distributed inference topologies, network-aware placement, prefill/decode disaggregation, checkpointing strategies that don't bottleneck
on storage or interconnect.

- Set the technical direction. Decide what we benchmark, what we adopt, and what we build ourselves. Bring the team along with strong writeups and reproducible
experiments.

What’s in it for you?

- Competitive salary (depending on the level of experience).

- Enjoy a flexible, remote-first global environment.

- Collaborate with a global team of cloud experts and innovators, passionate about pushing the boundaries of Kubernetes technology

- Equity options.

- Get quick feedback with a fast-paced workflow. Most feature projects are completed in 1 to 4 weeks.

- Spend 10% of your work time on personal projects or self-improvement. 

- Learning budget for professional and personal development - including access to international conferences and courses that elevate your skills.

- Annual hackathon to spark new ideas and strengthen team bonds.

- Team-building budget and company events to connect with your colleagues.

- Equipment budget to ensure you have everything you need.

- Extra days off to help maintain a healthy work-life balance.

Hiring process

- Screening call with Recruiter

- Hiring Manager interview

- Technical interview (system design)

- Live coding

- Culture Check interview with an executive

As part of our standard hiring process, we would like to inform you that a background check may be conducted at the final stage of recruitment through our third-party provider, Checkr.

title: Senior Applied ML Engineer | Kimchi (Model Router)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and the router deciding which model answers each request is ours too.

The Auto Router 

Our promise is one enforcement layer for your AI: budgets, spend attribution, and model routing, applied before a request ever hits a model. The Auto Router makes the call: for every request, which model serves it. Eight open-source models whose input prices span more than 20×, cached input up to 50× cheaper than fresh, frontier providers on customers' own keys, and a coding agent that fires hundreds of requests before its task is done. Frontier-level task success at a fraction of the token cost: that sentence is the product, and it stays true only if the model inside the router keeps getting better. That model is yours.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Every request gets a decision: which model serves it.

This is an applied-ML seat, not an infrastructure one. Platform engineers own the proxy, the streaming path, and the fleet. You own the model inside them: the training data, the objective, the evaluation, and the iteration loop that ships a better router every cycle.

The problem: routing is a prediction problem wearing a product's clothes. For every request you predict the quality each candidate model would deliver, what it would cost, and how fast it would decode, and you have to be right enough, in aggregate, that the savings are real and the quality never dips below frontier. The data is messy: rollout outcomes from benchmark harnesses, per-request records from the live fleet, override signals, and token streams whose speed depends on the serving concurrency at the moment. Speed itself is a correctness variable: on deadline-bound agentic work, a model that decodes three times slower doesn't do the same work slower, it does less work. That's why naive cost-per-token objectives quietly optimize for the wrong thing. And the bar for evidence is high: a router change ships only after production-parity evaluation with error bars, then gets held to its numbers in live traffic.

Stack: Python; PyTorch; SQL at scale (ClickHouse); OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM APIs; benchmark and rollout harnesses (RouterBench-class); GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've spent 5+ years in applied ML or ML research, and you've trained, evaluated, and shipped models that make real-time decisions (ranking, recommendation, bandits, pricing, or LLM routing) and you can tell that story with receipts.

- Strong Python and SQL at scale: you can pull, clean, and interrogate millions of request-level records without waiting on anyone.

- You know the difference between a model that got better and an eval that got easier.

- You have real opinions about what LLM benchmarks measure, agentic harnesses included.

- You know enough serving reality (TTFT, decode speed, batching, prefix caching, concurrency) to model the objective honestly.

- You instrument before you optimize, error bars and all.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

- Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

- Own the routing model end to end: features, objective, training, calibration, and release cadence. Iterate it like a product, not a research artifact.

- Build the evaluation that gates every change: production-parity benchmarks, router-vs-router comparisons, holdouts by task family, error bars on pass rates.
Nothing ships on vibes.

title: Senior Software Engineer (Trust)
description:
Beneath a simple yet elegant user interface lies a complex system of functionalities. Our AI-powered product uses advanced image recognition, facial verification, face recognition, facial anti-spoofing (liveness detection), and behavior analysis to make identity decisions. We help our partners build onboarding processes that ensure good people get things done and bad folks get stopped.

But knowing who someone is only gets you halfway. The next question is whether they can be trusted — and answering it means checking a person's identity data against the authoritative sources that hold the truth. Every country does this differently: a different registry, a different database, a different set of rules about what can be checked and how.

To take our platform to the next level, we're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Trust team. This team builds and operates the services that validate a person's identity data against country-specific authoritative sources — government registries, national databases, AML and sanctions screening — and turns that patchwork of very different upstreams into a single, dependable trust signal our customers can act on. Alongside sibling teams like Trust Registries and Trusted Documents, your work directly determines how many countries we can cover, how fast we can launch a new one, and how much our partners can rely on the answer we give them.

YOU'LL HELP US PROTECT HONEST PEOPLE ONLINE BY: 

- Designing, building, and operating Trust's backend services — the integrations with external identity data sources and the validation logic on top of them — with a strong focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability

- Expanding our global coverage: onboarding new countries and data sources quickly, and building the abstractions that make the next integration cheaper than the last one instead of more expensive

- Modelling messy, inconsistent upstream data into consistent, well-defined verification results — including the matching and validation rules that decide whether the data actually belongs to the person in front of us

- Making our systems resilient to upstreams we don't control — timeouts, retries and idempotency, backpressure, circuit breaking, graceful degradation, backwards-compatibility testing, SPOF elimination, and end-to-end monitoring of every provider we depend on

- Handling sensitive personal data responsibly, with regional data residency and compliance requirements designed in from the start

- Participating in on-call rotations, incident response, and postmortems to ensure our most critical checks stay healthy

- Driving engineering quality through code reviews, CI practices, runbook documentation, and mentoring teammates

YOU ARE THE RIGHT FUTURE VERIFFIAN FOR THE JOB IF YOU HAVE: 

- 5+ years of experience building large-scale backend applications with Python, including event-driven and async architectures with message queues (e.g. SQS, RabbitMQ, or similar)

- Hands-on experience integrating with third-party APIs at scale — and a healthy respect for what happens when they're slow, flaky, undocumented, or quietly change their response format

- Proven ownership of production-critical services — you understand what it means to be on-call and take reliability seriously

- Deep experience designing for resilience in distributed systems: idempotency, retries, backpressure, timeouts, backwards compatibility

- Strong data modelling instincts — you can turn heterogeneous, inconsistent external data into a clean domain model that holds up as the number of sources grows

- Strong understanding of modular design approaches and SOLID principles

- Hands-on experience building scalable, maintainable APIs

- Proficiency in a range of testing strategies that ensure robust and reliable software, including testing against external dependencies you can't fully control

- Solid understanding of relational database fundamentals

- Familiarity with structured logging and observability practices

- Strong communication skills — you can clearly articulate technical ideas to engineers and non-engineers alike, and work comfortably with Product, Compliance, and external data providers

NICE TO HAVE 

- Experience with identity verification, KYC/AML, financial services, or government/registry integrationsExperience working under data privacy and regulatory constraints (GDPR, regional data residency)

- Event-driven systems, workflow or orchestration engines, or Kubernetes

You can get familiar with our tech stack on StackShare .

Why Veriff ? 

We are the preferred identity verification platform partner for the world’s most innovative growth-driven organizations helping conveniently verify and safeguard users anywhere in the world. We support the broadest number of identity documents from nearly every country and territory in the world - and this is continually increasing! With a diverse team in the United States, United Kingdom, Spain, and Estonia, as well as robust backing and funding from investors including Accel, Alkeon, IVP, Tiger Capital, and Y Combinator, we’re dedicated to helping businesses and individuals build a safer and more secure world. We strive to be the benchmark for trust online, and we take pride in being a positive force.

title: Machine Learning Certification Researcher
description:
About the Role 

Imagine pioneering the mathematical and logical foundations that enable AI to fly safely in real-world, safety-critical aviation. As a Machine Learning Certification Researcher, you will address one of the most fundamental challenges in modern AI: proving that ML models are safe, reliable, and mathematically sound for deployment in autonomous flight. Your work will bridge the gap between cutting-edge statistical learning theory and formal aviation certification frameworks, building upon previous work (EASA CoDANN I and II, and FAA report DOT/FAA/TC-21/48), and putting real-world systems to the test.

At Destinus, we are shaping the future of defense through high-speed, autonomous flight technologies. We develop next-generation unmanned aerial systems that deliver greater speed, precision, and efficiency, supporting governments and defense organizations in mission-critical operations worldwide. Daedalean AG, the AI and autonomy hub of the Destinus Group, plays a key role in this vision—developing safety-critical AI systems at the intersection of advanced research and real-world aviation. Enabling machines to perceive, understand, and make decisions in real time, we combine aerospace engineering and artificial intelligence to build the next generation of autonomous flight systems, driving innovation where it matters most.

What You'll Do 

• AI Certification Strategy: Analyze our existing AI certification strategy and help adapt it—or pioneer entirely new strategies—to certify different supervised ML.

• EASA Framework Alignment: Connect mathematical guarantees, technical arguments, and model evaluations to the EASA W-shaped process for AI certification in aviation, ensuring our research aligns with the latest regulatory guidelines.

• Theoretical Foundation & Modeling: Conduct research into statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and mathematical guarantees for deep neural networks operating under dynamic real-world conditions.

• Uncertainty Quantification: Apply statistics and stochastic processes to model environmental uncertainties and sensor noise, and to quantify confidence in performance metrics.

• Literature & Proof Evaluation: Critically evaluate academic literature, mathematical proofs, and engineering assumptions with peer-review rigor to identify safety limitations and theoretical gaps in state-of-the-art AI.

• Regulatory & Audit Justification: Construct robust, logical arguments and technical justifications that translate complex, high-dimensional empirical data into structured evidence for safety audits and certification frameworks.

• Algorithmic Validation: Write clean, reproducible code in Python to test theoretical hypotheses, validate certification mechanisms, and benchmark model safety frameworks.

Requirements 

What You'll Need 

Machine Learning Theory & Mathematics 

• ML Theory & Statistical Learning: Deep understanding of statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and the mathematical foundations of deep neural networks.

• Statistics & Stochastic Processes: Strong background in advanced probability, statistical modeling, and stochastic processes.

• Python Engineering: Proficiency in Python with the ability to write clean, reproducible code (can also be learned on the job provided strong theoretical foundations and basic Python coding).

Research Rigor 

• Scientific Research Methodology: Demonstrated capability or background in conducting comprehensive literature reviews, identifying gaps in current state-ofthe-art AI, and synthesizing complex academic concepts into actionable engineering frameworks (can also be learned on the job if you possess a strong quantitative baseline).

• Peer Review Expertise: Ability or experience in the peer-review process—capable of critically evaluating mathematical proofs, algorithmic assumptions, and research papers to assess their validity and limitations.

Education 

• Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Theoretical Statistics, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related quantitative research field.

Who You Are 

• Critical Thinking & Healthy Skepticism: You possess a strong spirit of questioning everything. You naturally challenge conventional ML assumptions, probe for hidden edge cases, and refuse to take empirical accuracy at face value without rigorous proof.

• Logical Argument Building: You have an exceptional ability to construct robust, airtight logical arguments and technical justifications. You can translate complex empirical observations into structured, defensible evidence that satisfies strict 

engineering and regulatory scrutiny.

• Thrives in Ambiguity: You are motivated by hard, unsolved mathematical problems at the intersection of theoretical computer science, safety engineering, and real-world flight operations

title: Staff Applied AI Researcher (Agentic Search)
description:
About Nebius: 

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

We are seeking a Staff Applied AI Researcher to join a fast growing team building an agent native search platform - the web access layer for AI systems.

You can think of this as Google for AI agents: a system designed for machines, not humans. We are building agentic search, where AI systems actively plan, retrieve, evaluate, and refine information rather than simply returning results. As AI becomes the primary interface to the web, this layer will replace the role of traditional search engines.

We are designing how AI agents - not humans - retrieve, evaluate, and reason over web data in real time, under strict latency and reliability constraints. This means solving retrieval and ranking under entirely new access patterns and at significant scale, with systems operating over constantly changing, unstructured data and serving tens of thousands of production workloads 24 by 7.

This role comes with ownership over key parts of our applied AI research direction and system design, with a strong expectation of defining new approaches and shipping measurable impact in production.

What you'll work on: 

- Designing agent native retrieval systems optimised for machine consumption rather than human search UX

- Building systems where LLMs iteratively plan, query, refine, and reason over results

- Developing ranking and retrieval approaches for multi step, agent driven workflows under real world constraints

Your responsibilites: 

- Drive applied research and technical direction across retrieval and ranking systems

- Design and evolve multi stage retrieval architectures (query understanding, rewriting, reranking, iterative retrieval)

- Develop methods for grounding LLMs in real time web data at scale

- Define and implement new evaluation paradigms and metrics for agentic systems, where correctness is not reducible to clicks

- Lead experimentation on modern retrieval approaches (embeddings, hybrid search, reranking) and bring them into production

- Analyse trade-offs across relevance, latency, and cost at scale

- Work closely with engineering to deploy systems in high throughput, low latency environments

- Own ambiguous problems end to end and contribute to product and research direction

- Mentor engineers and help raise the technical bar of the team

Must haves: 

- 8+ years of experience in applied AI, ML, or software engineering

- Proven track record of shipping ML or AI systems to production at scale

- Deep experience with search, retrieval, ranking, recommendation systems, or assistants

- Strong understanding of modern deep learning, especially transformers and embeddings

- Experience with LLM integrated or knowledge intensive systems

- Experience designing evaluation frameworks and metrics for ML systems

- Strong programming skills in Python and at least one of Go, C++, or similar

- Ability to operate in a fast moving, product driven environment with high ownership and autonomy

Nice to haves 

- Experience with large scale search or recommendation systems

- Background in agentic AI systems (agents, tool use, autonomous workflows)

- Experience with RAG, multi step retrieval, or tool use

- Publications, open source, or similar signals of technical depth and impact

Benefits & Perks: 

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius: 

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

title: Product Owner
description:
Functieomschrijving 

Als Product Owner Interne Automatisering & IT ben jij de onmisbare brug tussen de business en ons IT-landschap. Je haalt de wensen en requirements op bij verschillende afdelingen en het Management Team, en vertaalt deze naar slimme, efficiënte automatiseringen. Waar anderen een complex proces zien, zie jij een kans om zaken sneller, beter en soepeler te laten verlopen. 

In deze rol schakel je veel met interne stakeholders om processen echt te doorgronden. Vervolgens bepaal je hoe we onze tools, waaronder ons ERP-systeem Odoo en Camunda, optimaal kunnen inzetten. Je werkt hierbij nauw samen met onze Applicatiebeheerder, die het functionele beheer voor zijn rekening neemt en onze Camunda/Python Developer. Omdat onze developer ook eigen projecten draait, is het fantastisch als jij zelf de taal van developers spreekt of zelfs je eigen Python-code kunt kloppen om snel iets te bouwen of testen. 

Taken en verantwoordelijkheden 

- Ophalen, analyseren en in kaart brengen van requirements bij diverse afdelingen en de MT-laag. 

- Vertalen van bedrijfsprocessen en wensen naar concrete automatiseringsoplossingen. 

- Beheren, prioriteren en structureren van de interne IT-backlog. 

- Samenwerken met de interne Camunda/Python developer en de Applicatiebeheerder om projecten succesvol en vlot op te leveren. 

- Adviseren van de business over procesoptimalisaties en nieuwe automatiseringskansen. 

- Zorgdragen voor een soepele implementatie en adoptie van nieuwe functionaliteiten op de werkvloer. 

Over Payter 

Bij Payter zijn we pioniers op het gebied van contactloze NFC- en cashless-technologie. Sinds 2007 maken we impact: we hebben het grootste Europese proefproject voor contactloze en mobiele betalingen gelanceerd, en sindsdien maken bedrijven over de hele wereld gebruik van onze oplossingen. We combineren innovatieve technologieën om veilige, duurzame en toekomstbestendige producten te ontwikkelen. Bij Payter krijg je de kans om bij te dragen aan slimme oplossingen die écht verschil maken in een snel veranderende wereld. 

- Je hebt hbo-werk- en -denkniveau en een sterke interesse in IT en bedrijfsprocessen.

- Je hebt (basis)kennis van Python; het is een hele mooie bonus als je zelf ook af en toe wat code kunt schrijven. 

- Je hebt bij voorkeur kennis van of interesse in ERP-systemen (zoals Odoo)

title: HIL Engineer — Huracan Rocket Engine
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

About the role

The Exploration Company is developing Huracan, a cryogenic rocket engine. The engine integrates e-pumps, power electronics, valves, embedded software, and control systems. We are seeking a Hardware-in-the-Loop Engineer to develop and operate HIL platforms for verifying the ECU, PDU, Valve Controller, inverter, electric pumps, and associated software. You will connect real hardware to real-time simulations, automate testing and data analysis, and develop emulator hardware for sensors, actuators, interfaces, and subsystem behaviour. 

You will verify nominal and fault conditions while ensuring test repeatability, traceability, and early fault detection. You will work closely with propulsion, embedded-software, power-electronics, control-systems, and hardware engineers to validate Huracan from simulation through laboratory testing.

Key responsibilities

- Design, build, and maintain the HIL test environment for our engine propulsion system, from engine controller board level up to the integrated propulsion subsystem 

- Define and implement the hardware and software architecture of the propulsion HIL bench, including signal conditioning, load and fault-insertion hardware, and real-time targets 

- Integrate real-time plant models (e.g., feed system, valves, pumps and motors, combustion chamber, thermal behaviour) into NI VeriStand and close the loop with the engine control unit 

- Emulate and simulate the sensors the controller depends on (e.g., pressure transducers, thermocouples and RTDs, flow meters, position and speed feedback) with flight-representative electrical characteristics 

- Emulate or integrate actuators and power electronics, such as valve drivers, motor inverters, igniters, and their control units, as real hardware, electrical loads, or models 

- Develop LabVIEW-based applications for desktop and real-time platforms (e.g., PXI, cRIO), including custom devices and bus interfaces (e.g., CAN, RS-422/485, Ethernet) 

- Implement fault injection at the electrical and model level to verify engine start-up, shutdown, and abort sequences as well as FDIR behaviour 

- Support test execution, data acquisition, logging, and automated reporting during verification campaigns 

- Validate and correlate simulation models against component-level and engine test data together with the propulsion team 

- Create and maintain technical documentation, including architecture specifications, interface definitions, model and code documentation, and user guides 

- Debug and troubleshoot across the bench, the models, and the unit under test, and continuously improve the test platform 

You will be in charge of 

- Delivering a robust and scalable HIL platform whose models, I/O configuration, and test sequences can be reused across engine configurations and projects 

- Running control loops and plant models deterministically at the rates the engine controller requires, using NI hardware, LabVIEW RT, and FPGA where timing demands it 

- Defining test automation workflows using NI TestStand and integrating them into the propulsion and system-level verification process 

- Coordinating closely with propulsion, avionics, and flight software engineers to ensure requirements traceability and test coverage 

- Keeping models, bench hardware, and test software under configuration control so that every test run is reproducible 

- Contributing to the continuous evolution of our HiL infrastructure, with an emphasis on performance, reliability, and maintainability 

- Ensuring all solutions meet space-grade quality and safety standards, aligned with project requirements 

Must-Have Skills and Qualifications 

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Control Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field 

- Hands-on experience building and operating HIL test benches for closed-loop control systems (e.g., engine, motor, or actuator controllers) 

- Proficiency in LabVIEW, including desktop and real-time application development 

- Hands-on experience with NI VeriStand in real-time test environments, including integration of simulation models (e.g., Simulink, FMU, or C/C++) 

- Experience emulating sensors and actuators at the electrical level (e.g., analog, thermocouple/RTD, frequency and PWM, discrete I/O) and working with motor drives or inverters 

- Familiarity with NI TestStand for test automation and execution management 

- Solid understanding of test platform architectures, hardware/software integration, and real-time systems 

- Strong debugging and troubleshooting skills, with a structured and methodical approach 

- Ability to write and integrate Python scripts to extend test workflows or support automation tasks 

Nice-to-Have 

- Experience with LabVIEW FPGA, for example for high-speed sensor emulation or motor and inverter simulation 

- Background in liquid rocket propulsion or in fluid and thermal system modelling 

- Experience with fault-insertion hardware and FDIR verification 

- Familiarity with ECSS standards or equivalent aerospace standards such as DO-178C 

- Experience supporting engine or integrated system test campaigns 

Why you should join us! 

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is: 

- We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

- We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them 

- We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?

title: Machine Learning Platform Engineer I
description:
Your Opportunity 

We are looking for a Machine Learning Platform Engineer to join Mollie's Machine Learning Platform team, sitting within our broader Data Domain. Our ML Platform empowers Machine Learning Scientists to develop and deploy custom ML solutions at scale across Mollie, serving domains including Risk & Fraud, Payments, Merchant Experience, Financial Services, Go-to-Market, and more. As the central team responsible for Mollie's Machine Learning Platform, we own the maintenance and continuous enhancement of the platform, ensuring it remains reliable, scalable, and fit for production-grade workloads. We work closely with domain teams to bring custom ML models into products, bridging the gap between research and real-world impact, while also designing and developing custom GenAI tooling and platforms for both internal employees and Mollie's customers.

This is a hands-on role where you will spend the majority of your time writing Python and Terraform alongside a team of skilled ML Platform Engineers. Based at Mollie's Lisbon Hub, you will be part of a geographically distributed team spanning Amsterdam and Lisbon, working in a collaborative environment that embraces both remote and hybrid ways of working.

What you’ll be doing 

As an ML Platform Engineer, you will:

- Collaborate closely with ML Platform Engineers, Machine Learning Scientists, and engineers across Mollie's domain teams to deliver scalable Machine Learning solutions

- Deploy and operationalize ML models to production in partnership with Machine Learning Scientists, bridging the gap between experimentation and real-world impact

- Enhance and maintain our cloud-based ML Platform on GCP, writing production-grade Python and Terraform daily

- Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for ML model training and inference, ensuring reliable and automated workflows across environments

- Deploy, manage, and scale model serving endpoints on Kubernetes, ensuring low-latency, high-availability inference for production workloads

- Assist in extending, developing, and hosting custom and open-source AI tooling ; enabling teams to rapidly build and deploy AI-powered solutions.

- Champion MLOps best practices, implementing standards around model versioning, experiment tracking, data validation, and automated retraining

- Ensure platform reliability by setting up observability, monitoring, and alerting for both infrastructure and deployed models

- Maintain and enhance open-source AI tooling hosted at Mollie (such as LiteLLM and LibreChat), and further support and expand our generative AI capabilities.

What you'll bring 

- 1+ year of experience deploying and maintaining ML models in production

- Good understanding of MLOps principles, including matters such as experiment tracking, reproducibility, pipeline automation, model versioning, and monitoring in production

- Strong hands-on Python programming skills, with proficiency across common ML and data libraries such as scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, XGBoost, LightGBM, and MLflow

- Familiarity with at a major cloud platform, preferably GCP

- Experience with containerization (Docker), with preferred familiarity in container orchestration tools such as Kubernetes and Kubeflow.

- Strong context-switching ability with sharp attention to detail, adapting quickly to shifting priorities

- Preferably familiarity with infrastructure-as-code (IaC) tools such as Terraform

- Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines for ML workflows

Grow your way 

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy. If you're excited by the idea of building what's next, for yourself and for thousands of businesses across Europe, we'd love to hear from you.

AI at Mollie 

We believe in Always Be Shipping, and AI brings that philosophy to life across every team, every role, every day.

AI is core to how we build. It helps us move faster, simplify work and make smarter decisions, creating real impact for the businesses we serve. We're looking for people who are excited to use AI to shape the future of finance with us.

description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. 
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

We are looking for an Analytics Engineer to join our Revenue, Purchase & Order Analytics Engineering team.

The area sits at the heart of some of the most critical customer journeys and commercial systems across Vinted’s Marketplace Business Unit, spanning Revenue (pricing and advertising), Purchase (inquiries and checkout), and Orders (transactions and fulfilment). Together, these domains create a rich, high-volume, and deeply interconnected data ecosystem.

As an Analytics Engineer, you’ll work at the intersection of data, engineering, and product, building trusted data products that power business and product decision-making across these domains.

In this position, you’ll 

- Build scalable data products: Design, develop, and evolve reliable, cost-efficient data products and pipelines that power analytics and machine learning use cases across the domains.

- Build quality in by design: Embed automated testing, validation, and quality controls throughout the data lifecycle to ensure data remains accurate, consistent, and complete.

- Strengthen observability: Improve monitoring and alerting to detect and address issues before they impact downstream consumers.

- Own production reliability: Take end-to-end ownership of production data systems, from investigating incidents and diagnosing root causes to implementing durable fixes that prevent recurrence and improve long-term resilience.

Who you’ll work with:

- Revenue, Purchase & Order Analytics Engineering: Join a talented and driven team of 7+ Analytics Engineers, working across interconnected domains and tackling complex, high-impact data challenges.

- Data & Decision Scientists: Work closely with Data Scientists and Decision Scientists to build trusted data foundations that enable better business and product decisions.

- Engineering, Product & Business: Partner with Backend Engineering, Product, and Business teams to understand their needs, shape technical requirements, and translate them into well-designed, trusted data solutions.

- The Analytics Engineering Guild: Be an active member of Vinted’s 40+ member AE Guild, benefiting from shared tooling, engineering standards, and knowledge across domains. You’ll also have opportunities to contribute to “side quests” that improve engineering practices, tooling, and reusable capabilities.

About you 

- Experience working as an Analytics Engineer, Data Engineer, or in a closely related data role.

- Strong SQL and data warehousing fundamentals, with the ability to build clean, performant, and maintainable data solutions.

- Hands-on experience with dbt or a similar data transformation framework, building well-structured and tested data models.

- Experience working with a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, or similar.

- A solid understanding of data modelling principles and their application to real-world analytical problems.

- Familiarity with workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow, Dagster, or similar.

- Comfortable working with high-volume, business-critical data, balancing a high bar for quality and reliability with a pragmatic bias for action.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to clearly explain technical concepts and trade-offs to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Work perks 

- The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme

- 25 days of paid annual leave

- Newest MacBook models

- Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family

- Frequent team-building events

- Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture

- NS Business Card for your commute to the office by public transport

- Work from Home allowance [[DELETE FOR Breda, Utrecht, Amsterdam Store]]

Als R&D Engineer Human Machine Teaming (HMT) ben je betrokken in de hele keten van onderzoek naar hoe intelligente en autonome systemen de mens kunnen ondersteunen in complexe taakomgevingen.

Als ervaren kracht verwachten wij dat je je comfortabel voelt in verschillende rollen en je moeiteloos beweegt tussen projectleiding, proposal management en onderzoek. Dit betekent dat je niet alleen het initiatief neemt tot nieuwe projecten maar ook de klantvraag uitwerkt en je inhoudelijk meewerkt aan projecten waarin je de voortgang bewaakt en proactief communiceert richting de opdrachtgever!

Je ontwerpt de interactie tussen gebruiker en geavanceerde systemen, ontwikkelt proof-of-concepts en demonstrators en/of beproeft wat wel en niet werkt in experimenten in onze simulatie- en XR-omgevingen.

Wat ga je doen?

Als R&D Engineer Human Machine Teamings bij NLR verken je voor uiteenlopende projecten innovatieve mens – techniek samenwerkingsconcepten. Soms zijn dit interne kennisontwikkelingsprojecten of Europese onderzoekscalls, ook werk je voor civiele klanten en defensie.

Je werkt daarbij samen met collega’s met uiteenlopende expertises, zoals Human Factors specialisten, UX-designers, Software ontwikkelaars, AI-experts en Onderwijsdeskundigen. Hierbij maak je gebruik van onze AR/VR, spatial computing en human-in-the-loop simulatieomgevingen. 

Een greep uit jouw werkzaamheden:

- Je bent bekend met de (on)mogelijkheden van de nieuwste AI-technologie, vergaard nieuwe kennis hierover, en bedenkt hoe dit ingezet kan worden om mensen te ondersteunen in hun dagelijks werk. Je bekijkt vanuit een technologisch oogpunt de interactie tussen mens en intelligente systemen. Hoe kan je een AI of automatisering zo ontwerpen dat het goed samenwerkt met de menselijke operator?

- Jij bedenkt en ontwerpt met je collega’s nieuwe samenwerkingsconcepten voor verschillende levels van autonomie en werkt deze uit in een testomgeving. Je begeleidt het (co-)ontwerpproces en softwareontwikkeling en evalueert het uiteindelijke resultaat in een operationele omgeving of gecontroleerd experiment. Uiteindelijk publiceer je de resultaten wanneer mogelijk in een wetenschappelijk tijdschrift.

title: DNA Synthesis Platform Engineer
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on scientist-engineer to help build our next-generation DNA synthesis platform, enabling high-throughput, cost-effective production of large and diverse DNA libraries. You'll work at the intersection of chemistry, materials science, bioengineering, and hardware development, designing and building prototypes, running experiments, and optimizing processes to turn new synthesis technologies into reliable, scalable production systems.

DNA synthesis is a fundamental part of our protein engineering platform. We're developing new approaches to dramatically increase synthesis throughput while reducing cost and turnaround time.

You'll work closely with our scientific and engineering teams to develop and prototype new DNA synthesis technologies. Your focus will be on translating scientific concepts into working hardware and experimental systems, designing and building prototypes, testing different approaches, and continuously improving their performance.

This is a highly hands-on, interdisciplinary role combining experimental science with practical engineering. You'll take ownership of prototype development, experimental validation, and process optimization, helping move promising technologies from early concepts to reliable, scalable systems.

We're looking for someone who enjoys building things, solving technical problems, and working across disciplines. You don't need to be an expert in DNA synthesis, but you should have strong scientific fundamentals, an engineering mindset, and experience turning ideas into working prototypes.

What You'll Do

- Design, build, and test prototypes for next-generation DNA synthesis technologies.

- Translate scientific and technical requirements into practical engineering designs and experimental setups.

- Scope and evaluate different technical approaches, components, materials, and equipment for prototype development.

- Develop and optimize the chemistry, materials, and processes underlying the synthesis platform.

- Design and execute experiments to characterize performance, identify limitations, and improve reliability.

- Work closely with mechanical, electronics, software, and automation engineers to develop integrated experimental systems.

- Troubleshoot complex technical problems across chemistry, hardware, and process engineering.

- Develop analytical methods and quality control strategies to measure performance and guide optimization.

- Help scale successful prototypes into robust, reproducible systems suitable for routine production.

- Work with external suppliers and engineering partners to source components, evaluate technologies, and accelerate development.

What We're Looking For

- A strong background in chemical engineering, chemistry, materials science, bioengineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field.

- Hands-on experience designing, building, and testing experimental setups, prototypes, or laboratory equipment.

- Strong understanding of chemistry, materials, or process engineering, with the ability to apply these fundamentals to practical engineering challenges.

- Experience developing and optimizing experimental processes, including systematic troubleshooting and performance characterization.

- Comfortable working across hardware and experimental science, translating scientific requirements into practical engineering solutions.

- Experience selecting components, evaluating technical trade-offs, and iterating on prototype designs.

- Strong experimental skills, including designing experiments, analyzing data, and making decisions based on results.

- Independent, resourceful, and comfortable working on open-ended technical problems.

- A practical, hands-on approach to engineering, with a focus on building, testing, and improving systems rather than purely theoretical development.

- Experience with DNA or oligonucleotide synthesis, including chemical or enzymatic approaches, is a plus.

- Experience with solid-phase synthesis, surface chemistry, or chemical process development is a plus.

- Familiarity with microfluidics, high-throughput dispensing, or array-based technologies is a plus.

- Experience with laboratory automation, instrumentation, or custom hardware development is a plus.

- Experience with CAD, electronics, fluidics, or mechanical prototyping is a plus.

- Experience scaling experimental technologies from proof of concept to production is a plus.

- Programming and data analysis experience, particularly in Python, is a plus.

- Start date: ASAP

title: Robotics Integration Engineer
description:

The next defining technological breakthrough will be in the physical world. We stand at a historical inflection point: bringing general-purpose intelligence into robotics.

At Enact we rethink the entire robotic tech stack from model architectures and data pipelines, to the actuators and sensors that feed the model. Pushing beyond pure vision and language approaches, we build a proprioceptive nerve system, and the cortex that makes sense of it, to solve dexterity through whole-body force-awareness and deploy robots for thousands of tasks in industry and beyond.

We are shaping a company where brilliant and unconventional people thrive together on solving the hardest challenges of our time. We are truth seekers. We reason from first principles, test our beliefs against reality, and trust that the best ideas can come from anyone. We move fast. We care deeply about our work and colleagues and are driven by passion to change the status quo.

If this resonates, we're excited to hear from you.

In This Role You Will 

- Design, integrate and test the electromechanical systems at the core of our dexterous robots: actuator modules, joints, and end-effectors, sensors, PCBs, and cable harnesses into compact, reliable units for high-DoF robotics

- Bring hardware to life: lead system assembly & bring-up, debug across mechanics, electronics, and firmware, and work with controls & AI engineers to build a fully vertically integrated manipulation system

- Develop & build automated test setups to validate performance, durability, and reliability, and take systems from prototype to series production

What We're Looking For 

- Degree (BSc/MSc/PhD) in mechatronics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field

- 3+ years of work experience developing complex mechatronic systems that bridge mechanical design, electronics, and software

- Solid understanding of electric motors, encoders, sensors, and motor drivers, and how to integrate them into a working system

- Hands-on experience with rapid prototyping, workshop tools, soldering, 3D printing, and prototype assembly/testing

- Fluency in English (spoken and written), with strong interpersonal and communication skills

Bonus Points If You Have 

- Hands-on development experience with high-DoF robotic systems (e.g., robotic arms, end-effectors, dexterous hands, or humanoids)

- Development experience with actuator systems (frameless motors, gearboxes, encoders, and integrated drives)

- Experience with PCB design or schematic review, and cable harness design

- Thermal management for compact, high-power electronics and actuators

What we offer 

- The opportunity to make a real impact working on some of the biggest challenges of our time

- A fast-paced learning environment alongside an outstanding, driven team

- Ownership from day one, with the ability to iterate quickly and see your impact firsthand in an early-stage startup

- Visa sponsorship & relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

- A world-class in-person setup in central Zürich, with excellent prototyping, robotics, and technical infrastructure for hands-on builders

title: Test Engineer Windtunnels (m/v/x)
description:

Ben je een teamspeler en een kartrekker, heb je een afgeronde HBO opleiding en ligt je interesse in de Lucht- en Ruimtevaarttechniek? Dan kijken wij uit naar jouw sollicitatie! 

Wat ga je doen?

Als test engineer ben je verantwoordelijk voor de verwerking, validatie en presentatie van windtunneldata aan de klant. Je werkt daarbij vanaf de start van een project tot en met de aflevering van windtunnel testresultaten nauw samen met klanten en collega’s. Bij de voorbereiding en uitvoering van de test weet jij de diverse meetgegevens en data te verifiëren, verwerken en presenteren aan onze klanten, zodat zij deze vlot kunnen interpreteren. Je werkt hiervoor samen met technici operators en projectmanagers. Je ontwikkelt multidisciplinaire kennis en doet ervaring op met het volledige proces, van data-acquisitie en geavanceerde meettechnieken tot de uiteindelijke verwerking en analyse van de data. Kortom een uitdagende baan waarbij er ruimte is voor eigen inbreng en je veel verantwoordelijkheid krijgt. Je werkt primair op onze locatie in Marknesse, waar wij twee lage snelheidswindtunnels beheren. Op projectbasis ondersteun je ook onze windtunneltesten in Amsterdam.

Wat breng je mee?

• Een brede technische opleiding (HBO) met kennis en ervaring op vlak van aerodynamica, instrumentatie en dataverwerking

• Kennis en praktische ervaring met data-analysesoftware, datavisualisatie en programmeren (bij voorkeur Fortran, Python)

• Collegialiteit, resultaatgerichtheid, leervermogen

• Je hebt de ambitie en potentie om je te ontwikkelen tot een gewaardeerd adviseur

• Ervaring met het verwerken van meetgegevens tot gewenste grootheden

• Scherp oog voor vragen van de klant en de doorvertaling naar passende oplossingen

• Flexibiliteit om (op projectbasis) ook onze windtunneltesten in Amsterdam te ondersteunen

• Uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden in Nederlands en Engels, kennis van het Duits is een pré

Wat bieden wij jou?

Werken bij NLR, betekent werken in een nationale en internationale hightech omgeving. Samenwerken en betrokkenheid staan bij ons hoog in vaandel. Door jou vrijheid en eigen verantwoordelijkheid te geven, ben jij het best in staat om tot baanbrekende innovaties te komen. Wil jij jezelf vakinhoudelijk én op persoonlijk vlak ontwikkelen? Ook dat kan bij NLR als lerende organisatie, met daarnaast een opleidingsbudget, een mentor, interne coaches en goede contacten met mbo’s, hbo’s en universiteiten.

Naast dit alles bieden wij jou:

- De kans om bij te dragen aan complexe en maatschappelijk relevante vraagstukken;

- Voldoende vakantie- en ATV-dagen (in totaal 45 bij fulltime dienstverband) voor een goede werk-privébalans;

- Een eindejaarsuitkering van 8%;

- Een tegemoetkoming in jouw zorgkosten;

- Extra betaald ouderschapsverlof;

- De mogelijkheid om jezelf te ontwikkelen met opleidingen en cursussen die passen bij jouw ambities.

Jouw nieuwe werkomgeving

De Duits-Nederlands Windtunnels (DNW) exploiteert windtunnels op vier verschillende locaties van het Nederlands Lucht- en Ruimtevaartcentrum (NLR) en van de Duitse zusterorganisatie DLR. In deze zeer geavanceerde installaties wordt hoog gekwalificeerd onderzoek verricht voor internationale opdrachtgevers, voornamelijk uit de luchtvaart en automotive sector. Wij werken aan projecten waarbij de aerodynamische, aero-akoestische en aero-elastische eigenschappen van vliegtuigen, helikopters, treinen en (vracht-) auto’s worden gesimuleerd en gemeten.

De afdeling Projects and Customer Relation Management is verantwoordelijk voor de acquisitie en uitvoering van projecten in de windtunnels. Het team bestaat uit diverse R&D engineers en project engineers met expertise op het vlak van aerodynamica, aero-akoestiek, meettechnieken en mechanical engineering. Ook speelt de afdeling een belangrijke rol in de kennisontwikkeling en het business development proces van DNW. Het team opereert in en rond diverse windtunnels in de vestigingen Amsterdam en Marknesse.

Wat betekent werken bij NLR?

Koninklijke NLR is al ruim 100 jaar een kennisorganisatie met de wil en ambitie om te vernieuwen. Vanuit die drijfveer maken wij de wereld van lucht- en ruimtevaart veiliger, duurzamer, efficiënter en effectiever en staan wij voor baanbrekende innovaties.

Bij ons werken meer dan 1000 gedreven professionals, van vliegtuigbouwkundigen tot psychologen en van wiskundigen tot applicatiedeskundigen. NLR staat voor een inclusieve en diverse organisatie waar iedereen zich welkom, veilig, gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelt. 

Wil jij meer weten?

Mail met onze recruiter Danielle Kuijf; collega’s vertellen jou graag hoe het is om bij NLR te werken. Vergeet trouwens ook niet eens een kijkje op onze socials te nemen zoals ons YouTube kanaal . 

Solliciteren?

Mooi, we zijn benieuwd naar jou! Stuur je motivatiebrief en CV via de ‘Solliciteren’ button. 

Een integriteitstest en het verkrijgen van een VOG zijn voorwaarden voor indiensttreding.

Acquisitie wordt niet op prijs gesteld!

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
Join our mission 

We're proud to work with many incredible companies, accelerating their ability to build their products. 

We've spent years watching talented engineering teams lose momentum to the same frustrating bottleneck: waiting. Waiting for CI to finish. Waiting for builds to complete. Waiting for tests to run.

After experiencing this pain firsthand at companies of every size, we set out to build the developer infrastructure platform we'd always wanted to use. Something that would seamlessly integrate with our workflows and the tools teams already love—but make everything dramatically faster and more cost-effective.

Today, we're already accelerating hundreds of companies around the world, helping them ship features instead of waiting for infrastructure. We've built something that feels almost magical in its simplicity: change your runs-on line, mount your toolchain cache directory and suddenly your builds are 5x faster.

About the role 

Namespace's approach is low-friction, designed for immediate integration into existing developer toolchains, empowering teams to experience tangible results within just five minutes. With an end-to-end stack optimized for high performance—including compute, memory, storage, and networking—Namespace delivers capabilities and efficiencies unmatched by traditional cloud providers.

As a DevOps Engineer at Namespace, you'll build and operate the infrastructure that makes this performance possible. You'll own the compute, storage, and networking behind every build our customers run, keeping the platform fast, reliable, and cost-effective as we accelerate more companies around the world.

Our culture 

We're looking for people with grit—people who push through ambiguity, take ownership, and keep going when things get hard. You're deeply curious, driven to understand how things work and how they can be improved. Most importantly, you have a strong bias to execution: you don't wait for perfect conditions, you ship, learn, and iterate quickly. What you'll do 

- Own the reliability, performance, and scalability of the infrastructure that runs every customer’s build, test, and CI job on Namespace.

- Optimize performance across compute, memory, storage, and networking.

- Automate provisioning, deployment, scaling, and recovery across our fleet.

- Build observability, alerting, and incident response processes that identify and resolve issues before they affect customers.

- Drive capacity planning and cost efficiency, so we continue to deliver infrastructure that is both faster and more cost-effective.

- Collaborate closely with product engineers to ship new capabilities quickly and safely.

What we're looking for 

- Strong engineering fundamentals and hands-on experience operating production infrastructure at scale.

- Deep knowledge of Linux, networking, and storage, plus experience with tools like Kubernetes, Terraform, or similar.

You can expect: 

- Competitive salary and stock options

- Market-leading parental leave

Life at Namespace Labs: 

- We pride ourselves in being a small team of experts that can achieve a lot.

- We balance our long-term vision with short-term pragmatism.

- We believe in being fully transparent internally on how decisions are made, on how the company is doing, and we use that information to drive our decisions.

title: Technical Support & Operations Engineer
description:
Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include the most energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges. 

Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions 

Join Us at the Forefront of Quantum Computing Innovation 🚀 

About the Role 

As part of the continued growth of our activities and the deployment of our photonic Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) to international customers, we are looking for a Technical Support & Operations Technician / Engineer to join our team.

You will contribute to the operational monitoring of Quandela's QPUs and other hardware products deployed at customer sites , ensuring their proper operation and supporting maintenance activities, both remotely and on site.

Working at the interface between Quandela's technical teams and system users, you will develop a broad understanding of our products, particularly the interactions between hardware equipment and software control interfaces. You will perform initial technical investigations when issues arise and involve the relevant technical experts when required.

The role combines technical support, maintenance, field interventions, training and continuous improvement in a complex and international technological environment.

Internal training will provide you with the specific knowledge required to understand our technology and systems. No previous experience in quantum computing is required. 

As our support and maintenance activities are still being structured, you will also contribute to improving our processes, tools and operational methods.

Your Key Responsibilities: 

System operations & technical support 

You will contribute to maintaining the operational performance and availability of QPUs and other hardware products deployed at customer sites.

- Monitor the operation and performance of installed systems.
- Analyse operational data and identify anomalies or performance degradation.
- Perform initial technical investigations to characterise issues and help determine the appropriate resolution path.
- Follow up on technical incidents and corrective actions with the relevant teams.
- Maintain accurate technical records of systems and interventions.
- Provide remote technical support to customers and trained personnel working on the systems.

Maintenance & customer-site interventions 

You will contribute to the preparation and follow-up of preventive and corrective maintenance activities.

- Track maintenance schedules and anticipate upcoming interventions.
- Identify the resources, equipment, spare parts and technical expertise required for each intervention.
- Perform diagnostic, maintenance and system recovery operations according to established procedures.
- Support technicians and technical experts remotely or on site during interventions.
- Perform functional checks and testing following maintenance activities.
- Track completed actions, outstanding issues and upcoming maintenance requirements.
The role involves business travel within France and internationally , with frequency and duration depending on the needs of our installed systems. 

User training & technical guidance 

You will help customers and technical operators become increasingly autonomous in operating and maintaining our QPUs.

- Train users and technical operators on routine QPU operation and maintenance activities.
- Support users in operating the systems and their control interfaces.
- Share best practices for operation, troubleshooting and maintenance.
- Contribute to the creation and improvement of training materials and technical documentation.

Documentation & continuous improvement 

You will ensure the traceability of technical operations and contribute to structuring our support and maintenance activities.

- Prepare technical monitoring, intervention and maintenance reports.
- Maintain up-to-date technical documentation for installed systems.
- Contribute to writing and improving diagnostic, maintenance and operating procedures.
- Capitalise on field experience to improve reliability and facilitate future interventions.
- Contribute to implementing tools and methods for the structured monitoring of our installed systems.

Requirements 

Education & experience

- Associate's, Bachelor's or Master's degree in instrumentation, applied physics, optoelectronics or a related technical field.
- The position is open to both experienced technicians and engineers with a strong interest in hands-on, operational activities .
- Previous experience in operations, system integration, maintenance or technical support for complex systems is preferred.
- Experience working in a multidisciplinary hardware/software environment is highly valued.
- Experience supporting or maintaining technical equipment installed at customer sites would be an advantage.

Technical skills Required 

- Good understanding of complex technical systems combining hardware and software.
- Knowledge of electronics, instrumentation and/or control systems.
- Ability to analyse operational data and characterise technical issues.
- Ability to perform diagnostic and maintenance operations according to established procedures.
- Ability to identify and involve the appropriate technical experts when required.
- Strong organisational skills and ability to rigorously track interventions, deadlines and outstanding actions.
- Ability to follow, write and improve technical procedures.
- Professional fluency in English, both written and spoken , as you will interact directly with international customers and colleagues, deliver training sessions and produce technical documentation.
- Willingness and ability to travel internationally.
Nice to have

- Knowledge of optics, photonics and/or cryogenics .
- Hands-on experience with optical systems, including basic optical alignment.
- Experience operating or maintaining cryogenic systems.
- Basic programming or scripting skills, particularly Python .
- Experience maintaining scientific or industrial equipment.
- Experience delivering technical training to users or operators.
Benefits 

- Competitive salary, flexible based on your experience 
- Profit-sharing & company savings plan
- 100% health coverage (Alan)
- 50% transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus
- Meal vouchers (Swile), Gymlib fitness support
- Childcare assistance & referral bonuses (€1,000–€2,000)

What we offer

- A meaningful role with real ownership, from day one
- A team eager to collaborate and grow with you
- A hybrid work model (3 days/week onsite in Massy, 1 day in Paris, 1 to 2 days remotely)
- Daily exposure to the entire quantum stack — from high-level APIs to low-level firmware, and everything in between.
